note: v1 91.27 (seeds 0/11 91.27/91.08), first draft of an APOCALYPTIC SPOKEN-WORD SUITE, 'Leave the Lights On' (Godspeed-style), 7:50 in five movements at 70 bpm, E minor. I Static: wind and tape hiss, and a narrator close in the room (wM's speech voice) reading a last letter - 'this is the last broadcast. if you can hear this, leave the lights on.' II Procession: cellos, a glockenspiel playing THE SIGNAL (B-G-A-E), a clean guitar cascading into a dotted-eighth echo, an e-bow. III Signal: an earned crescendo in five eight-bar stages - toms and ride, bass, tremolo guitars and strings, then kick, snare and the e-bow theme, a sub under it. IV Fire: two chug rigs left and right, fuzz bass, a tape-echo lead on the theme, the drums doubling at the end; the wall tape-stops into V Ash: rain, the theme on a music box in E MAJOR, and the narrator once more, closer: 'leave the lights on.' One theme, transformed five times; levels 100 (-12.8 LUFS, TP -2.1). (The voice was a radio at first; the radio is chirper-two's opener, so it became a narrator.)

v2 92.91 (seeds 0/11 92.91/92.71 vs v1 re-scored 93.47/93.31): THE DOOR OPENS - Harry's 'filter sweeps in builds' and 'sidechains' notes, carried over from Soft Concrete. The Signal movement's long crescendo now also happens in the filter: the whole mix sits behind a low-pass at 4 kHz as the drums arrive and opens a little at each eight-bar stage, wide open on the downbeat of the Fire, so the build is heard as distance closing - the band walking towards you - rather than only getting louder. In the Fire the strings and the tape-echo lead breathe against the kick (a slow sidechain pump). Kept slightly below the stored best on purpose (the darker build reads as spectrum 94 -> 88; a 2 kHz start cost twice that and was eased); levels 100.

v3 93.01 (seeds 0/11 93.01/92.83 vs v2 92.91/92.71): THE LETTER - Harry's 'synth'd speech', given room to tell something. The narrator no longer stops after the opening lines: over the Procession, between the glockenspiel's theme and the cascading guitar, he reads on, a sentence every few bars with the music breathing between them - 'the city is quiet now.' 'the buses stopped at nine.' 'someone left a radio on in an empty room.' 'and every window is lit.' - each with a falling, sentence-final intonation, so the long instrumental build that follows has a world to belong to (the album's title, said at last). Measured as loud as the music around it (the difference sits at the passage's own level), so it is foreground, Godspeed-style.
